'''''Carex riparia''''', the '''greater pond sedge''', is a species of [[Cyperaceae|sedge]] found across [[Europe]] and [[Asia]]. It grows in a variety of wet [[habitat]]s, and can be a dominant species in some [[swamp]]s. It is Britain's largest ''Carex'', growing up to {{convert|130|cm|ftin|abbr=on}} tall, with glaucous leaves up to {{convert|160|cm|ftin|abbr=on}} long. It hybridises with a number of other ''Carex'' species, including the closely related ''[[Carex acutiformis]]'' – the lesser pond sedge. A [[variegation|variegated]] [[cultivar]] is grown as an [[ornamental grass]].

==Distribution and habitat==
''Carex riparia'' has a broad [[range (biology)|distribution]] over [[Europe]] and [[Western Asia|Western]] and [[Central Asia]], with isolated occurrences in [[North Africa]].<ref name="GRIN">{{GRIN | accessdate=May 11, 2011}}</ref> It can form large stands along slow-flowing rivers, canals, on the edges of lakes, and in wet woodland.<ref>{{cite book |editor1=C. D. Preston |editor2=D. A. Pearman |editor3=T. D. Dines |year=2002 |title=New Atlas of the British and Irish Flora |chapter=''Carex riparia'' |author1=M. J. Y. Foley |author2=M. S. Porter |page=722 |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |isbn=978-0-19-851067-3}}</ref> It may be the dominant species in [[swamp]]s, especially if there is [[standing water]] in spring, and is also found in [[tall-herb fen]]s, alongside ''[[Carex acutiformis]]'', ''[[Carex acuta]]'' and other similar species.<ref name="Jermy"/>

==Description==
[[File:Carex riparia (Ufer-Segge) IMG 22812.JPG|thumb|left|Ripe utricles]]
''Carex riparia'' was [[species description|first described]] by [[William Curtis]] in his 1783 work ''[[Flora Londinensis]]''.{{#tag:ref|Many North American sources erroneously attribute the species to [[Moses Ashley Curtis|M. A. Curtis]].|group=Note}}<ref name="GRIN"/> It is easily confused with ''[[Carex acutiformis]]'', the lesser pond sedge, but can be told apart by its greater number of male [[Spike (botany)|spike]]s, which grow close together at the top of the [[culm (botany)|culm]].<ref name="Jermy"/>

The [[leaf|leaves]] of ''C. riparia'' are up to {{convert|160|cm}} long by {{convert|6|-|20|mm}} wide, [[glaucous]], and narrowing at the tip to a trigonous point.<ref name="Jermy"/> The stems are {{convert|60|-|130|cm|abbr=on}} tall, rough, and sharply triangular in section,<ref name="Jermy"/> making ''C. riparia'' Britain's largest species of ''Carex''.<ref>{{cite EB1911|wstitle=Cyperaceae |volume= 07}}</ref> They bear 1–5 female spikes, each nearly cylindrical and generally overlapping with the next, and 3–6 more densely arranged male spikes.<ref name="Jermy"/> Each female spike is {{convert|3|-|10|cm|abbr=on}} long, often with some male flowers at the tip, while male spikes are {{convert|2|-|6|cm|1|abbr=on}} long.<ref name="Jermy"/> The [[fruit]]s of ''C. riparia'' are [[Utricle (fruit)|utricle]]s, {{convert|5|-|8|mm|1|abbr=on}} long, with an inflated ovoid shape. They taper to a distinct, bifid beak, which bears three [[Stigma (botany)|stigmas]].<ref name="Jermy"/>

''Carex riparia'' is known to [[hybrid (biology)|hybridise]] with a number of other sedge species, including ''Carex acutiformis'' (forming ''Carex × sooi''), ''[[Carex lasiocarpa|C. lasiocarpa]]'' (forming ''C. × evoluta''), ''[[Carex rostrata|C. rostrata]]'' (forming ''C. × beckmanniana''), ''[[Carex vesicaria|C. vesicaria]]'' (forming ''C. × csomadensis''), ''[[Carex elata|C. elata]]'' and ''[[Carex flacca|C. flacca]]''.<ref name="Jermy">{{cite book |author1=A. C. Jermy |author2=D. A. Simpson |author3=M. J. Y. Foley |author4=M. S. Porter |year=2007 |title=Sedges of the British Isles |edition=3rd |series=BSBI Handbook No. 1 |isbn=978-0-901158-35-2 |publisher=[[Botanical Society of the British Isles]] |chapter=''Carex riparia'' Curtis |pages=304–306}}</ref>

==Horticulture==
''Carex riparia'', particularly the [[cultivar]] 'Variegata', is used as an [[ornamental grass]] in gardens with wet soils.<ref>{{cite book |author=John Simmons |year=2008 |title=Managing the Wet Garden: Plants that Flourish in Problem Places |publisher=[[Timber Press]] |isbn=978-0-88192-900-3 |chapter=''Carex'' |pages=[https://archive.org/details/managingwetgarde0000simm/page/188 188]–190 |url=https://archive.org/details/managingwetgarde0000simm|url-access=registration }}</ref>
